newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Slow start to expiration week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Slow start to expiration week.

text.p: Some big volume crossed, but overall, major U.S. stock index options trading was subdued on the first day of May expiration week, traders said Monday.
"It's kind of a ho-hum day," one trader said.
One index options trader said he expected activity to pick up as the week unfolds, particularly in the S&P 100 index, where a large number of in-the-money call contracts remain open.
Lawrence McMillan, publisher of the Daily Volume Alert newsletter, said in a report that the large open interest in the in-the-money OEX calls could push the market higher.
"If this open interest continues to be in place as the week progresses, that should reflect itself as arbitrage buying pressure," he said in the report.

But he added that it was too early to say for sure whether buying pressure linked to the expiration would emerge because the arbitrageurs can either roll their positions to longer dated options or exercise them.
In late trading, the OEX May 810 and 820 calls were most active, with turnover of roughly 19,500 and 15,000 contracts, respectively.
The May 810 call had open interest of 23,640, which included an addition of 1,666 on Friday. The May 820 call had open interst of 27,792 and was reduced by 349 on Friday.
On the put side, the May 790 traded 10,330, the May 815 traded 10,205 and the May 810 traded 10,215.
Traders said some investors were rolling positions out of the May series into June and July, but largely in small numbers.
The OEX June 810 call was the busiest OEX June option, with volume of 1,440. The June 805 put traded about 1,170.
The OEX July 790 call and put traded 1,500 and 1,530 contracts, respectively.
The OEX spot index was ahead 15-1/2 points at 824.
The S&P 500 index rose 13-1/2 to 838 and June S&P 500 futures were 13.85 points at 843.50.
The market's rally failed to drive index options volatilities much lower and traders said that was partly a reflection of investor expectations of continued sharp moves.
The Chicago Board Options Exchange's volatility index, priced off specific OEX contracts, was up 0.16 at 22.06. It ranged between 21.07 and 22.94.
